PASSES, not hidden: (1) one store is genuinely versioned -- SyntheticUser carries schemaVersion (current 2), load() accepts 1...2, and SyntheticUserTests prove a v1 payload (legacySignals removed) loads, out-of-range and missing versions are rejected; (2) the DecisionPointRecorder JSONL file store has a real legacy v1/v2 step-up migration (migrateLegacyRecords) and writes atomically; (3) AppState has one flag-guarded one-off migration (AlarmKit v1.3.0). FAILURES: SwiftData / ModelContainer / VersionedSchema / SchemaMigrationPlan / Core Data / CloudKit all appear ZERO times. Persistence is 39 distinct UserDefaults keys with 11 files decoding Codable blobs from defaults (memories the user wrote, liked quotes, synthetic-user record, nudge stats, habits, personalisation profile) -- user content inside the preferences store, no inventory, no recorded storage decision. Only SyntheticUser payloads carry a version; it has NO step-up transform (range-check + nil), so the first required-field change silently nils every existing record, and a newer payload read by an older build is overwritten by a fresh record on refresh(). Every other store decodes with try? into an empty state: no Logger/analytics on the failure paths checked, no quarantine/backup/quarantine key anywhere (grep backup/quarantine/corrupt/lastKnownGood: zero), and the next persist() overwrites the same single key -- loss is silent and permanent. No last-known-good or pre-change copy, no restore path. App, widget and notification service share an App Group suite, but the shared payloads are unversioned. No continuity decision for reinstall/device change (iCloud/CloudKit zero; local-only by accident). Deletion code exists in AppState but is not verified against all keys/suite/files. Migration tests exist only for SyntheticUser; no corruption rehearsal and no record-count preservation check exist for any store. NOTE: source read of an unreleased branch, not a device test; whether onboarding answers also exist server-side is outside this tree and unverified -- the local stores above are what the app itself reads at launch.
